name: GET /api/events/stream - Server-Sent Events push channel
description:
STREAMING ENDPOINT - NOT A REQUEST-RESPONSE CALL (MUST-63). This route responds 200 with Content-Type text/event-stream and then HOLDS THE CONNECTION OPEN indefinitely, writing frames as changes occur. A normal test asserting a JSON body would hang until timeout, so the happy-path case asserts ONLY the handshake: status 200 and the event-stream content type. Everything after the handshake needs a streaming client and cannot be driven by the HTTP runner.

STREAMING CONTRACT for whoever consumes it. On connect the server writes a ': connected' comment frame so a client can tell 'connected and quiet' from 'never connected'. Thereafter each change is one frame: 'event: <type>' followed by 'data: {"type","subject_id","at"}' and a blank line. A ': heartbeat' comment frame is written every 25 seconds to defeat proxy idle timeouts; comment frames carry no data and are ignored by EventSource. The four event types are lead.captured, lead.routed, lead.reassigned and routing_rule.changed.

EVENTS CARRY NO STATE BY DESIGN. Each one means 'something changed, re-read' — the client re-fetches the projection, which remains the source of truth. Delivery is at-most-once with no persistence or replay, so an event emitted while a client is disconnected is simply lost; that is safe only because no client correctness depends on receiving one. SINGLE INSTANCE ONLY: subscribers live in the serving process's memory, so behind more than one replica a client on replica A never sees an event published on replica B. The durable cross-instance path is the transactional outbox owned by the composition-layer epic.

AUTH: protected like every other read, because the stream names leads and owners. Note the route is deliberately NOT wrapped in asyncHandler — that helper forwards a rejection to the JSON error handler, which would try to write an error body onto a response whose headers are already committed as text/event-stream.

testCases.name: Open the stream and assert the handshake only

errorCases.when: the Authorization header is absent, or present without a Bearer token. Rejected by the guard BEFORE the stream headers are written, so this failure is an ordinary JSON error response
the bearer token fails verification or has expired
